items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: I said, Mr. Harris. That was my barber.

ctx.x: And he started to cutting on my hair and got one side up, and his mother came in, and he hadn't washed the dishes. So he had to leave me in the bathroom. So -- my mother's here. He went to wash the dishes and try to take care of his chores, and I had to slip out the front door when he let me know when to go. And when my mother came home that night, she asked me, did I get a haircut. I say, sure, lying.

She said, who cut it? I said, Mr. Harris. That was my barber. Uh-huh. Are you sure Mr. Harris cut it? Yes, he did. She didn't say anything to me now other than I couldn't go to the Emancipation Park the next day because I lied to her. And she told me one thing. She said, I can't stand a liar because anybody that'll lie will steal, and I can't stand a liar and I can't stand a thief.

And she punished me. She didn't whip me for it. She punished me by not letting me go, and everybody left me the next day, but I told the lady next door that we were ready -- my mother was ready for her, and she called my mother on the job where she was working, and she said, I'm sorry he told you, but he didn't tell me. And she wouldn't let me go. But she begged and pleaded for me, but it didn't work.
